description: Verification (CV) mode coverage: CV deploy (RT-CV + Behavior Analytics containers) + Workflow A onboarding of the ladder sample + the VLM-verifier config path, and that an incident query in CV mode routes to the Alert Bridge incidents endpoint directly (not /generate) and reports whatever it returns grounded (empty or populated are both valid — rtvi-vlm runs in CV mode too). The CV-owned store is `mdx-vlm-alerts-*` (behavior/alert-kind verified events, NO REST query endpoint) — probed best-effort via Elasticsearch :9200 for verdict-schema fields. Does NOT test realtime rule CRUD in CV (gated to real-time mode). Requires a verification-mode deploy (vss-rtvi-cv + vss-behavior-analytics).

expects.query: Deploy the VSS alerts profile on {{platform}} in verification (CV) mode (i.e. `/vss-deploy-profile -p alerts -m verification`) using remote LLM and remote VLM endpoints. Then onboard the ladder sample so the CV pipeline has PPE content to detect: obtain the `sample-warehouse-ladder.mp4` NGC sample video (one of the bundled sample videos — if it is not already in NVStreamer's streamer_videos, fetch it via the vss-manage-video-io-storage sample-data bootstrap), upload it through NVStreamer (port 31000) as a sensor named `sample-warehouse-ladder`, then register in VIOS (port 30888) the RTSP URL exactly as NVStreamer's streams API returns it (query NVStreamer for the served URL — do NOT hand-construct a host:port URL, and include BOTH keys in the `/sensor/add` payload — `sensorUrl` (the returned URL) and `name` (`sample-warehouse-ladder`); without the `name` key VST silently names the sensor `SENSOR`). In CV mode, registering the sensor in VIOS is the entire onboarding step — the CV pipeline auto-picks up the stream; do not look for a separate 'create alert' API. Do NOT finish until the VSS Agent REST API (`curl -sf http://localhost:8000/docs`) and VIOS (`curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list`) respond successfully and `sample-warehouse-ladder` is listed — wait and retry for a few minutes if a service is still starting.
checks: `sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 12 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:8000/docs >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (VSS Agent REST API responsive; polls up to ~3 min to absorb deploy readiness timing).
`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx vss-rtvi-cv` returns exit 0 (CV perception / Grounding DINO — required and present in verification (CV) mode).

`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx vss-behavior-analytics` returns exit 0 (Behavior Analytics is the CV-only mode signal — its presence confirms the deployment is verification (CV), not VLM real-time).

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 18 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list 2>/dev/null | grep -qi sample-warehouse-ladder && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (sample-warehouse-ladder onboarded into VIOS; in CV mode this VIOS registration is the whole Workflow A onboarding — the CV pipeline auto-attaches; polls up to ~1.5 min to absorb fetch/upload/registration delay).

`curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:9080/api/v1/verification/config` returns HTTP 200 with a JSON list of alert-type verifier configs, including a ladder/PPE-related `alert_type` (the CV VLM-verifier prompt config that Workflow B / references/verification.md customizes) — confirms the CV verifier-config path is populated and queryable in verification mode.

expects.query: What alerts have been triggered today on sample-warehouse-ladder?
checks: The agent routes this 'what happened' incident query to Workflow C and queries Alert Bridge directly: the trajectory issues a `GET http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents` (optionally scoped to sample-warehouse-ladder or today's window) — it does NOT use the VSS Agent `POST /generate`, and its ANSWER is sourced from the `/incidents` response, not from the bare active-rules list (an incidental read-only `GET /api/v1/realtime` peek is tolerable; answering the incident question with the rules inventory is the failure).

`curl -sf --max-time 15 'http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/incidents?limit=5'` returns HTTP 200 with a body matching the Alert MS `IncidentListResponse` contract — top-level `status`, an `incidents` array, integer `count` and `total`, and a `timestamp`. Deterministic contract probe; an empty AND a populated `incidents` array are both valid outcomes (rtvi-vlm runs in CV mode too, so incident-kind events may land in this store; behavior/alert-kind verified events go to `mdx-vlm-alerts-*` instead).

The agent's final reply is grounded in the `/incidents` response it actually received: it reports the incidents found (sensor/time-scoped) or states none were found when the response is empty — it does NOT fabricate incidents, does NOT answer from memory, and does NOT fall back to presenting subscription rules as the answer.

CV-scope data-plane probe (best-effort, the store CV verification actually writes): `curl -sf --max-time 15 'http://localhost:9200/mdx-vlm-alerts-*/_search?size=5'` returns HTTP 200 with a well-formed Elasticsearch search response. IF it contains hits, the documents carry CV verification fields in their `info` block — a `verdict` of `confirmed` / `rejected` / `not-confirmed` / `verification-failed` (or empty when a pluggable parser is used) and a verification response code (`verificationResponseCode` or `verification_response_code`) — accept camelCase or snake_case. Zero hits is an acceptable pass (CV detection latency); the verdict-schema assertion applies only when documents are present.
